title: The Murder of Jane Stanford
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck examine the 1905 poisoning and death of Jane Stanford, co-founder of Stanford University, following a listener suggestion. They cover the Stanfords' background and fortune from the Central Pacific Railroad, the death of their son Leland Stanford Junior, the founding of the university, and early conflicts with president David Starr Jordan over micromanagement, spiritualism, and the firing of Edward A. Ross. They then describe the first poisoning attempt with rat poison in San Francisco, the fatal strychnine poisoning in Hawaii in February 1905, the coroner's jury verdict of murder, Jordan's cover-up via Dr. Waterhouse's report, and later investigations by Robert W. P. Cutler (2003) and Richard White, who suspected secretary Bertha Berner. The episode closes with listener mail about a laser drone episode and a joke about the hosts' employer.

entities.name: The Mysterious Death of Jane Stanford

segments.title: Opening banter and listener suggestion
segments.summary: Hosts introduce a true crime murder mystery episode suggested by a listener, teasing that the victim is Jane Stanford.

segments.title: Stanford family background and fortune
segments.summary: Background on Jane Lathrop Stanford and Leland Stanford, their upstate New York roots, Leland's dry goods business supplying prospectors, and the Big Four's Central Pacific Railroad fortune, along with their horse farm in Palo Alto and the death of their son Leland Junior at fifteen.

segments.title: Leland Junior's death, Bertha Berner and spiritualism
segments.summary: Leland Junior dies at fifteen. Bertha Berner becomes Jane's secretary and inherits a large sum. Jane pursues spiritualism to contact her son, and medium Maud Lord Drake is linked to the founding of the university.

segments.title: Founding of Stanford University
segments.summary: Stanford University opens October 1, 1891 with free tuition, co-education, and practical programs. Jordan is hired as president; hosts note his eugenics and pacifist views.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before continuing the Stanford story.

segments.title: Jane's control of the university and conflicts with Jordan
segments.summary: After Leland Senior dies, Jane becomes sole trustee, wins a lawsuit over railroad debts, and gives a $10 million endowment with strict controls. She caps women students at 500, clashes with Jordan over spiritualism, William James, Julius Goebel, and fires professor Edward A. Ross, causing an academic freedom scandal.

segments.title: First poisoning attempt in San Francisco
segments.summary: In January 1905, Jane is given water with rat poison at her San Francisco home; she drinks some, induces vomiting, and the secretary also tastes it. Lab tests confirm poison. Jordan works to suppress the poisoning story.

segments.title: Local investigation and private detective
segments.summary: Local media and police question servants, including a Chinese cook, but no charges result. A private detective hired by the university suggests a servant framed another, and the matter is dropped. Jane travels to Hawaii with Berner and maid May Hunter.

segments.title: Fatal strychnine poisoning in Hawaii
segments.summary: On February 28, 1905, in Waikiki, Jane asks Berner for baking soda water, becomes ill, and dies about thirty minutes later after strychnine poisoning symptoms; local doctor Francis Humphreys attends.

segments.title: Coroner's jury verdict and Waterhouse cover-up report
segments.summary: Jordan and trustee Timothy Hopkins travel to Hawaii with San Francisco detectives. A coroner's jury rules death was poisoning on March 8. Jordan then brings in Dr. Waterhouse, whose report blames heart failure from overeating and indigestion, and the local doctor and police are angered.

segments.title: Accusations and press coverage
segments.summary: Jordan blames the Hawaiian doctor and police and defends Berner in San Francisco, which the press accepts. Local papers cover investigations for about a month, with no charges filed.

segments.title: Cutler's 2003 book and the 2026 reinvestigation
segments.summary: Stanford neurology professor Robert W. P. Cutler's 2003 book The Mysterious Death of Jane Stanford reexamines the evidence preserved in Hawaii, the autopsy by seven doctors and a toxicologist, and Jordan's letter suggesting alternative theories, implicating Berner as a possibility.
topics: The Mysterious Death of Jane Stanford

segments.title: Richard White's Who Killed Jane Stanford and motives
segments.summary: Historian Richard White's book Who Killed Jane Stanford points to Bertha Berner, citing her inheritance and her constrained life, while suggesting Jordan covered up the death to protect the university and the endowment.

segments.title: Aftermath of the case
segments.summary: The hosts note the case was never solved. Jordan remained president until 1913 and Berner died in 1945; her two biographies of Jane Stanford revealed little.

segments.title: Listener mail about laser episode and conspiracy joke
segments.summary: A listener named Dan notes a laser episode aired the day after news of a laser drone takedown at El Paso Airport; the hosts reply jokingly and invite more emails.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing credits for Stuff You Should Know, a production of iHeartRadio.
